content.text:
Here are three papers on evaluating RAG systems. My search turned up nothing from 2026, so these are from 2024–2025 and may not be the newest work.

1. **"Evaluation of Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Survey"** (Yu et al., May 2024, arXiv 2405.07437). It proposes the RAGR framework (Retrieval, Generation, Additional Requirement) for analyzing RAG benchmarks. It also covers the limits of current benchmarks and future directions.
   - [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.07437v1)

2. **A survey of RAG evaluation in the LLM era** (2025, arXiv 2504.14891). It discusses why the hybrid retrieval-plus-generation design makes evaluation hard. I only saw a search snippet for this one, so I haven't confirmed the exact title or authors. The authors may be Gan et al.
   - [papers.cool listing](https://papers.cool/arxiv/2504.14891)

3. **"BERGEN: A Benchmarking Library for Retrieval-Augmented Generation"** (Rau et al., Findings of EMNLP 2024). It is a library for running standardized RAG experiments, and it also analyzes existing RAG metrics and datasets.
   - [ACL Anthology](https://preview.aclanthology.org/dashboard/2024.findings-emnlp.449)

I can search again for 2026 papers specifically, for example on arXiv, if you want newer ones.
